decision: Do not remove selected tests based on runtime PASS. Preserve published selector; timings and phase reporter remain research-only. No full metadata tracing implemented.
findings: Current runtime_probe complete/failing/finished fields alone cannot distinguish PASS from skipped execution. Child-local experimental phase reporting closes only this reporting ambiguity.
Executor test explicitly requests get_context("spawn"); changing it to fork would alter test semantics. Existing overlay correctly returns incomplete for child process creation.

Ordinary executor baseline costs 80.049303 CPU seconds at host affinity10 and 44.493635 CPU seconds at explicit affinity2, both exceeding observed 13.423-18.258 second marginal CI savings per selected commit.
Generator memory test has potential arithmetic benefit (1.615606499 cold CPU vs 3.343-6.686 marginal CI seconds), but isolated PASS is not sufficient correctness evidence.
Parser max_nodes costs 21.873645907 cold CPU and is absent from the captured 30 sample selections.
A cold passing test can fail after an earlier test or shared fixture changes state. Passing isolated and full-suite executions are different claims.
Overlay read_text observes patched bytes but Path.stat sees original baseline file size. A metadata assertion can pass in the overlay and fail on a physically patched filesystem.

methodology.baseline_patch: Exact-text replacement of first sqlglot/__init__.py line; overlay source bytes remain unchanged.

container.timing_caveat: Local amd64 emulation and concurrent workloads differ from the scoring host; these are measured observations, not promised server timings.

methodology.cpu: Initial overlay measurements use process_time; subprocess creation is prohibited there. Plain pytest measurements sum RUSAGE_SELF and RUSAGE_CHILDREN after worker pools join.
methodology.explicit_pass: All requested nodes collected and finished; setup/call/teardown report passed, including all subtests; no skips, xfail, failures, errors, incomplete overlay or unloaded patched Python modules.
methodology.plain_baseline: Normal pytest execution with real spawn ProcessPool support, no patch overlay. Same source and catalog node.
methodology.selection: Top three tests sorted by supplied catalog duration, minimum 5 seconds; no patch IDs or answer labels used.

bytecode_reflection.observation: Also explicitly reads each typing-module source before comparing annotator code objects.

filesystem_metadata.observation: Path.stat().st_mtime_ns reads generated expected extension files in temporary build directories, not an obvious pinned production-source stat reader.

import_loader_distinction.implication: A future explicit stat-dependency collector can start at os.stat/Path.stat without automatically wrapping this particular low-level loader path. Other loader/collection calls still require separate evidence; do not blanket-exclude them.
import_loader_distinction.observation: importlib._bootstrap_external._os is posix. With only os.stat wrapped, _path_stat emitted zero wrapper calls while explicit Path.stat emitted one.

non_executable_match.observation: Comment discussing missing __code__ on compiled functions.

pinned_source_audit.scope: Read-only rg search over pinned tests/ and sqlglot/ Python sources for stat metadata and bytecode/source introspection; limited textual audit, not proof of absence.

remaining_soundness_gaps: Shared-state test ordering, session/class fixtures, caches, registration side effects, and collection scope can differ between one-node probing and the official full suite.
Virtual patch metadata (stat size, modification times, related filesystem operations) is not fully virtualized.
Native-extension filesystem accesses are not universally guaranteed to emit Python open audit events; absence of an unsupported report is not a full native I/O proof.
The probe collects specified nodes rather than reproducing every full-suite import and fixture interaction.
